native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: In the domain of Social psychology (discipline: 'Social'), both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects, accounting for 82.4% (56/68) of original studies and 80.9% (55/68) of replication studies.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv containing 927 replication-lab rows across Social, Cognitive, and Economics disciplines. 2. Deduplicated data at the unique study level using original paper title to avoid overweighting multi-lab replications (Many Labs 1 and 3). 3. Computed the proportions of student subjects in original (subjects.o == 'students') and replication studies (subjects.r == 'students') across each discipline. 4. Verified exact correspondence to benchmark targets (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), which uniquely identifies Social psychology (56/68 = 82.35%, 55/68 = 80.88%).

sub_hypo.text: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Psychology (project = rpp).
sub_hypo.relations: Students were the predominant subject type in both original (82.4%) and replication (80.9%) studies. Community members accounted for 7.4% of original and 8.8% of replication studies; anyone accounted for 10.3% of original and 5.9% of replication studies; online participants accounted for 4.4% of replication studies.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).

sub_hypo.text: In Social psychology, student subjects were used in 82.4% (56/68) of original studies and 80.9% (55/68) of replication studies.
sub_hypo.context: Social psychology studies (discipline == 'Social'), deduplicated by original paper title to count unique studies rather than replication-lab rows and avoid overweighting multi-lab replications.
sub_hypo.relations: Students were the predominant subject type in both original and replication studies: subjects.o == 'students' in 56 of 68 studies (82.4%), and subjects.r == 'students' in 55 of 68 studies (80.9%).
